_note: ENG-10/GAME-10a: one Foamer spec per type. `test` is the shared base spec every type starts from (the name is kept: the F01 tests read it directly). `types` holds one entry per type with only what differs from the base: its rig id in data/foamer-rigs.json and its attacks. An attack's `token` is the director pool it draws from; its `needs` are parts that must still be attached; its `range`, when it has one, is how far its reach is measured to (default: an attack with a melee token uses the base attackRange, one with a ranged token the preferred distance). The three *DistanceMetres fields belong to the base so every spec has them; only a ranged type reads them: the distance at which it stops walking in and keeps the ring (throwRangeMetres), the distance it tries to keep and throws from (preferredDistanceMetres), and the distance it backs off to when the player closes inside it (retreatDistanceMetres).

partDamage._note: Per part kind. hpShare: the part's health as a share of the Foamer's (at least minHp). hit: multiplies dart damage to the part. total: share of that damage that also comes off the Foamer's health. CONTENT-PLAN 3.1 and 3.2.

catastrophic._note: Pop when the damage from popTypes dart types in the last window seconds is at least share of max health. No starter dart type pops (Paul, 2026-11-01): heavier darts and blaster mods add theirs.

chunk._note: GAME-09b: the chunk finish. A blaster or mod with a chunk block, a hit inside its rangeMetres, qualifies when the killing shot's own damage on this Foamer inside the window above is at least minShare of max health, and the rig's tier is in tiers or the Foamer is already finishable (finishWeakened). Then carveRadius is carved as a sphere at the shot's mean hit point, up to debrisMax foam chunks burst out of the hole, and it goes down with the hole in it, pushed chunk.push times the ragdoll's kill push. Pops are unchanged.

finisher._note: GAME-07. weakenShare: when health first falls to or below this share of the max, the Foamer is finishable and staggers for weakenStaggerTime instead of stagger.time (a part break still gives the short stagger). reach: melee finishers work this far from the eye. coneCos: the view cone's cosine, the aim must be inside it. total: the finisher's lasting time. turnTime: the share of total the view spends turning onto the Foamer. CONTENT-PLAN 3.1 and 3.2: the finisher always pops.

ragdoll._note: ENG-12. density in kg/m^3 for the part cuboids. damping slows the fall to a limp, heavy foam feel. keepStride: share of a walking Foamer's speed its parts keep when it dies (the stride feeds the fall without deciding it). killSpeed: the killing shot tips the Foamer over about its feet, away from the shooter: every part gains this speed in m/s along the shot's horizontal direction, scaled by its height over the top of the body (feet barely move, the top moves most), so it falls without being thrown. limits: hinge range in radians about the part's local x axis, per part kind, measured from the pose it had when it went down (negative bends forward).

handicaps._note: GAME-11. someLegsSpeed: ground speed with some legs gone but still enough to walk. noLegsSpeed: with none left. noHeadTurnRate: turn rate scale with no head. fallBelowLegs: a living Foamer left with fewer legs than this falls over. crawlSpeed: crawl speed as a share of the rig speed. crawlLength: the lying capsule's length as a share of the rig height. fall: the fall is an inverted pendulum about the foot it still stands on, a in radians from upright and a'' = (gravity / pivotHeight) * sin(a). startTilt: the tilt it starts from, so it tips at once. proneTilt: the tilt it lands at. sideShare: share of the tilt that is roll toward the lost leg, the rest is forward pitch. bounce: share of the landing angular speed it bounces back with, once. settle: seconds at rest after the bounce before it crawls.

F05._note: GAME-10b: the Darter. attackRange is its bite; the charge line and speed are in charge, and the brain reads rangeMetres. The chest and brow plates shrug off darts and carve little; the orange back weakpoint takes extra. No upright attack besides the charge: with no legs it is prone, so only bite is left.

charge._note: GAME-10b: the charge. speed m/s, metres the longest run, rangeMetres where a charge may start, holdMetres the ring it circles on without a token (so it charges from range), telegraphSeconds the scrape before it (stops, head down, dust), wallStunSeconds the stagger after a wall (back open), playerStunSeconds how long a player it runs into cannot move. plateStopsShield and plateArcDeg: a shield charge into the front plates bounces off instead of staggering the Darter.

armour._note: GAME-10b: per part id. damage multiplies the kind's hit multiplier; carve scales the dart carve radius (the plate chips slowly).

F03._note: GAME-10d: the Swarmer. Weak point: none. Health 2 comes from its rig (it pops in one or two hits). nibble is its whole attack: a short windup, hit and run. pack is how many a pack spawn makes; the swarm ring and gaps are in data/ai.json pack. The type reads its own speed and health from the rig.

F04._note: GAME-10e: the Blocker. Holds a shield wall: slots side by side at slots.holdMetres, a volley over the shield with the ranged token. The shield is armour on the shield part, but only across its arcDeg front: a side or back dart takes full damage, and a staggered Blocker has the shield down. shieldChargeTime is the stagger the player shield charge leaves it in (a longer one than the base).

slots._note: GAME-10e: the shield wall. Blockers walk to a line across the player at holdMetres, one slot each spacingMetres apart; an index past the ends of the line spreads the wall.

armour._doc: GAME-10e: the shield. A front dart chips it slowly and does almost nothing; arcDeg is how much of the front it covers. Out of the arc, or with the shield down (stagger), full damage.

attacks._note: GAME-10e: range pins the volley's reach, so a Blocker on its slot (the hold distance) is inside it and fires over the shield.

line._note: GAME-10e: the line the range spawns for the F04 type choice, so one press shows the wall. inboundSteps: a blocked slot slides outward this many slots before the member is skipped.
